The PR reports an extracted host executable, but no FAIL-first output from the actual regression target. Run the filtered tests with `Err(_) => panicked = false`, then restore the code and attach both outputs. This establishes that the committed tests catch discarded worker failures.

⚠ Failure context: [crates/gpu-gates/src/bin/gate_gemm.rs:2987](https://github.com/midagedev/bloomery/blob/f11aaeea0fdd634d0e735f9cc9f684e70304e0f8/crates/gpu-gates/src/bin/gate_gemm.rs#L2987). Every worker panic caught here returns `reference thread panicked`. The callers propagate it before printing the current case, layout or shape. Retain those inputs through the existing diagnostic path, or identify a retained probe that reports them. Adding that context while these callers change makes later failures easier to reproduce.

### Checked

Duplicates: 4 new functions checked against existing reference and failure helpers; no duplicate owner found. No dryer pairs were supplied.

Silent failure: 3 worker-result sites followed; both fabricated-result fallbacks are removed, and all 5 consumers propagate the error to `exit_with`.

Tests: static mutation check only. Ignoring the panic at line 2983 would fail both new 32-value tests' error assertions. Returning an empty success at line 714 would fail the K-quant test's error assertions. Making `exit_with` return success on errors would fail the shared assertion. Tests were not executed during this review.

Adversarial checks: partial work, all-work and initializer panics return errors; successful joins cannot mask a later panic. Zero slots retain the explicit empty-result contract. The recipe filter matches all 3 tests and preserves failure status.

Gates: no bands, thresholds, count pins or existing cases changed. Hot path: none; the changes affect gate reference work.
